description: Sulfuryl fluoride -- the gas a house is tented with for drywood termites, vented to the open air at the end of every job and lasting some 36 years there -- has a GWP100 of 4630 in IPCC AR6 Table 7.SM.7. ecoinvent's v3.12 implementation of EF 3.1 added that number 'following IPCC 2021' (§15.3.1, Table 19); EF 3.1 states nothing for the substance under any climate category, though it characterises it for freshwater ecotoxicity in all thirteen of its contexts. So the factor reached `queue/proposed-factor`, and `lcia-factor-rulings.json` adopts it, as ecoinvent's own statement of the IPCC's number. It reaches only the two air compartments ecoinvent has a flow for; the four this list carries from EF 3.1's flow list stay empty, which is #151's follow-up and not this claim's business. The claim that urban air stays empty was here until #152 filled it, which is what that expectation was written for.

expectations.title: A kilogram of sulphuryl difluoride to unspecified air is worth 4,630 kg CO2-eq
expectations.comment: The compartment an inventory writes to when it does not say where the emission went, which for a substance released by opening a tent is most of them. Before the ruling this list published nothing here and the gas scored zero. `derivation` is claimed alongside the number because the two are different facts: 4630 could in principle arrive as a restatement of a twin, and this one arrives because somebody signed for it.

expectations.title: The same kilogram is worth 4,630 under `Climate change-Fossil`
expectations.comment: ecoinvent files this substance in `climate change` and `climate change: fossil` and in neither of the biogenic or land-use sub-categories, which is what a synthetic fluorinated gas of industrial origin should do. Both items are ruled, so both are claimed; a ruling on one and not the other would publish a substance into the aggregate and not into the sub-category that adds up to it.

expectations.title: Both of the air compartments ecoinvent states a number for are published

subject.context_display: Environmental → Air → Medium stack, <150 meters → Rural (<1000 people/square mile)

expectations.comment: ecoinvent's `air / non-urban air or from high stacks`, which this list's context vocabulary calls a medium rural stack. Named separately from the compartment above because a ruling is keyed on the substance and category rather than on a flow: it should reach every flow the implementation spoke about, not the first one.

expectations.title: ecoinvent's 4,630 is still published as ecoinvent's
expectations.comment: Adopting a number does not absorb it. The transcription stays published under the name of whoever made it, so a reader can see that this list's number and ecoinvent's are the same number rather than two arrivals at one answer.

expectations.title: The JRC states no climate factor for this substance, and the list does not invent one for it
expectations.comment: The silence that made this a proposal rather than an agreement, and it has to stay legible after the ruling. If EF 3.1 ever states a number here the question is a different one -- two implementations disagreeing, or agreeing -- and `ruled_about` sends it back to the queue rather than letting this decision stand over it.
